ccrs.title: California Crash Reporting System (CCRS) open data

methods.what: Police-reported crashes from CCRS (CHP), all severities including property damage only. Deleted reports dropped; the newest report version kept; preliminary reports flagged.
cite: Sec. 2.1: SWITRS/CCRS as the statewide crash repository

methods.what: Default: the last 5 complete calendar years (1-10 allowed). Open: end on the last finalized CHP year, and warn under 3 years (#34 items 8, 15).
cite: Sec. 2, p. 14: at least 3, preferably 5 years
Ch. 10: typically three to five years

methods.what: Each crash counted once at its most severe outcome: K fatal, A suspected serious, B suspected minor, C possible, O property damage only. Injury crashes with no reported level are kept as U and disclosed (#34 item 12).

A crash within 250 ft of a study intersection's center is assigned to that intersection; when two intersections compete, the nearest wins. Other crashes within the corridor buffer go to the segment they fall in.
cite: Sec. 2: crashes within 250 ft of an intersection center are attributed to it; closest intersection when centers are under 500 ft apart
Part C, Sec. C.6.2: intersection vs. segment crashes

methods.what: Segments run from intersection center to intersection center; this is the length used for per-mile figures and segment rates.
cite: Part C, Sec. C.6.2: a segment begins and ends at the center of an intersection

methods.what: Crashes CHP flags as freeway (IsFreeway) are excluded from an arterial study and reported by rule. Open: an include option for ramp-terminal studies (#34 item 9).
Shown only where AADT is entered. Intersections: crashes per million entering vehicles (MEV = entering vehicles per day x 365 x years / 10^6). Segments: crashes per 100 million vehicle-miles.
Today: major-road AADT + minor-road AADT (right for a 4-leg intersection with two-way leg AADTs). Open: 3-leg intersections use major + minor/2, and the inputs need a stated definition (#34 item 11).
cite: Ch. 4, Eq. 4-2: TEV = total entering vehicles per day

methods.what: Not provided; the PDF says so. Open: critical-rate test against similar sites, or TASAS averages on state highways (#34 item 7).
cite: Ch. 4, Sec. 4.2.3: critical rate from the average rate at similar sites
compare with the average intersection; build jurisdiction averages
Sec. 3.1, p. 23: compare with similar areas around the state

methods.what: Excess proportion of specific crash types: each location compared with locations of the same kind on the corridor (intersections with intersections, segments with segments), HSM variance and beta prior, ranked by excess proportion. A binomial test is used, and labelled, when the reference group is too small.
cite: Ch. 4, Sec. 4.2.3 and 4.4.2: excess proportions of specific crash types
Ch. 10: only similar location types analyzed together
high-proportion screening; P = 1 - betadist(p*, a + x, b + n - x)

methods.what: A draft pattern library from the HSM diagnosis step, labelled draft until the engineer approves it (#34 item 6).
cite: Ch. 10: collision diagrams and pattern identification

methods.what: Not built (#52). Weight = crash cost of the severity / PDO crash cost; FHWA publishes current KABCO crash costs.
CrashIQ is a site (hot-spot) analysis of one corridor; the findings name crash types that systemic countermeasures also target.
cite: Sec. 1.6: combine spot and systemic approaches

methods.what: Intersections and traffic control come from OpenStreetMap; the engineer reviews and edits them on the Corridor step.
